Corpus rule T-2 forbids this and names debug logs explicitly, and A1 requires following the corpus export contract, so A1 is not delivered. The same line is a side effect in an exported function, which also breaks the 'every exported function is pure' clause of contracts/api.md. Nothing in the spec calls for logging here.

findings.text: I-1 is not satisfied at this head even though its witness is green. The journey lane's `export` record passes at this head's tree (1e965c01), which matches the executable check, but the gate message still lists the observation as none. I-1 is anchored only at T-1, while its statement requires the export contract as a whole, and the T-2 breach leaves that unmet. A passing `export` record therefore does not show T-2 compliance. T-1 itself holds: the id is returned verbatim.

directives: Remove `console.debug(input.token)` from packages/xenon/src/vessel-export.ts, and do not log the token anywhere else. Keep `return { vessel: input.id }` unchanged.

Extend packages/xenon/test/vessel-export.test.ts through the real vesselExport entry point so that it fails if the token reaches a log. For example, capture console.debug, log, info, warn and error (or the stdout and stderr writes) during the call and assert that the token never appears. Confirm the new assertion fails against the current implementation before removing the log line. Keep the existing vessel assertion.
Regenerate goldens with `node tools/gen-goldens.ts` after the fix, and do not hand-edit them. The signature should not change, so goldens/xenon.json should stay as it is at this head.
